mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and economic momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with INDPRO > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 jobs signals labor market weakening, which historically precedes negative equity market performance over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS falls by more than 50,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strong housing demand and inflationary pressure, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than 12 consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >12 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% for >12 months and inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.3% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing momentum, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during four consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 0% monthly growth signals a deteriorating labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS monthly change < 0%.
